records.title: Consultancy: Mid-Term Review of the BELIEVE Project.
records.summary: Background CBM Global Disability Inclusion is seeking a consultancy firm to undertake the mid-term review of the Bungoma Enhancing Localised, Inclusive, Efficient, Vision Engagement (BELIEVE) Project. BELIEVE is a KES 79 million inclusive eye health project implemented in Bungoma County by InterChristian Fellowships’ Evangelical Mission (IcFEM Mission), through Dreamland Mission Hospital, in partnership with the County Government of Bungoma, Organisations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs) and other health, rehabilitation and referral partners, supported By CBM Global Disability Inclusion. The project runs from March 2025 to December 2027. Its interventions cover improving accessibility of eye health services, community eye screening and treatment, referral and follow-up, rehabilitation, provision of assistive devices and psychosocial support, economic empowerment for specified groups, community-led advocacy, health-system strengthening and organisational capacity development. Project objectives Overall objective To contribute towards reducing the burden of preventable blindness in Kenya. BACKGROUND The Refugee Consortium of Kenya (RCK) is a public benefit organization established to respond to the protection, rights and justice needs of refugees, asylum seekers, internally displaced persons, other forcibly displaced populations and host communities in Kenya. Over the years, RCK has evolved from a primarily service-oriented organization into an increasingly influential national actor working across protection, justice, governance, peace and social justice, women and girls’ empowerment, mental health and psychosocial support, institutional development, advocacy and systems strengthening. RCK’s current Strategic Plan 2023–2027 was developed around the vision of “A just and inclusive society for all the displaced and host populations”, with a mission to protect and promote the well-being, voice and dignity of displaced and host populations. Its strategic goal is to promote a safe environment in which displaced and host populations access justice and protection and are empowered to achieve their full potential. records.title: Fieldwork Consultancy for the SGBV Care Pathway Study (Addis Ababa)
records.summary: Tiko Africa Ethiopia invites qualified consultants or firms to carry out a mixed-methods study on screening, service readiness, quality of care and access barriers along the SGBV care pathway for adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) aged 15–24 in Addis Ababa. The consultant will lead the study from data collection through analysis and reporting. 1. Background Tiko is an African non-profit organisation addressing the “Triple Threat” facing adolescent girls and young women in Sub-Saharan Africa: early pregnancy, HIV and sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV). The Triple Threat package, delivered through Tiko’s technology-enabled, community-driven platform, is Tiko’s standard programme in all of its intervention areas. In Addis Ababa, Tiko supports screening, care and referral for survivors of SGBV, and for young women identified through transactional or survival sex screening under the Dignified Livelihoods Initiative (DILI), which adds livelihood support to the Triple Threat package. records.summary: The SMART (Multisectoral Strategic Action on Food Security and Protection for Strengthening Resilience) Project is an integrated resilience and protection initiative implemented by AVSI Foundation and Somali Lifeline Organization (SOLO) in Dadaab and Fafi Sub-Counties of Garissa County. The project seeks to strengthen the resilience of refugee and host communities while improving access to essential protection services for women, children, refugees, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable populations affected by protracted displacement, poverty, protection risks and recurrent climate-related shocks. Under Outcome 2, the project aims to strengthen community-based protection systems and improve access to quality protection services through a combination of capacity strengthening, referral system enhancement, community mobilization, awareness raising, and stakeholder engagement. The intervention is grounded in a prevention and response approach that seeks to strengthen community awareness of rights, available services, protection risks and reporting mechanisms while promoting positive social norms, inclusion, accountability and social cohesion. records.summary: REQUEST FOR CONSULTANTS The Adventist Development and Relief Agency (ADRA) is a global humanitarian organization with a mission to work with people in poverty and distress to create just and positive changes. ADRA Somalia belongs to the worldwide network, comprised of more than 130 supporting and implementing country offices. ADRA Somalia is seeking to recruit a consultant for strengthening community-based climate resilience through integrated climate change, adaptation disaster risk reduction, early warning and systems and anticipatory action. Somalia continues to face multiple and interconnected challenges, including protracted conflict, recurrent droughts and floods, displacement, environmental degradation, poverty, and increasing pressure on livelihoods and essential services. These challenges have heightened the vulnerability of communities to climate-related and other disasters, particularly among women, children, older persons, persons with disabilities, internally displaced populations, and other marginalized groups.
